transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Time: 11:00 AM PDT / 18:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Derek Huang (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (Greenline Eng Mgr), Liam O'Connor (Greenline SRE), Priya Rao (Greenline Product)

Summary (auto): quick perf review after last week's tuning; focused on function-calling stability, KV cache behaviour under burst, and JSON schema failures. Agreed next steps to run controlled load tests and exchange configs + sample contracts.

Topics: perf numbers, batching / kv cache, function-calling contracts, graceful degradation, security/KMS question, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining on time, we'll try to keep to 45, 50 tops. quick roll call?
[00:14] Maya (Greenline): hey Maya here, priya and liam are on as well.
[00:20] Liam (Greenline SRE): yeah hey, liam here. little late on the perf numbers but we pulled some runs.
[00:28] Derek (Redwood SE): cool, i'll share screen in a sec — i put the tuned batching and kv cash notes in the doc, forgive me, kv cash, um cache, speech to text is funky sometimes.
[00:40] Speaker 4: morning all.
[00:45] Samira: ok high level — since last week we bumped batch size, enabled prefix caching and switched quantized variant for the mid-tier model. we saw p95 drop but p99 still clumpy under bursts. want to walk through the runs.
[01:05] Maya: that's correct. the staging runs show steady throughput 130 reqs/s but occasional p99 spikes ~ 1.2s to 1.8s which impacts the UI.
[01:20] Derek: i can show the trace — over here you can see during bursts the KV cache lookup hits drop, which forces repeated early token compute. i suspect cache TTL alignment with our token chunks is off.
[01:38] Liam: small thing — our front-end expects sub-800ms tail latency. Is that realistic for the quantized mid-tier?
[01:48] Derek: under normal traffic yes, but bursts we need to either reduce batch wait or increase parallel capacity. tradeoff is cost.
[02:05] Priya (Greenline Product): can you explain more about batch wait? we got confused between Redwood "batching" and our API batching.
[02:16] Samira: absolutely — there's two layers: client-side orchestration around bundles of prompts, and Redwood server-side continuous batching. increasing server batch window can improve throughput but hurts single-request latency.
[02:32] Speaker 4: and there was some mis-match in our invoke pattern too, right?
[02:37] Derek: yes, the particular pattern where you do function-calling followed by immediate new prompt hits cold kv state. when function returns and you re-invoke, the kv cache vanished because of chasing small TTLs.
[02:52] Maya: hmm that shows in our error logs — we saw malformed JSON outputs about 0.7% of calls. sometimes the model returns a slightly different key name like "user_email" vs "email_address".
[03:06] Samira: this is where structured output and strict JSON schema help. derek will demo the function-calling contract enforcement and a small schema validator you can run client-side.
[03:19] Derek: ok demo time — (screen-share noise) so here's a simple function contract: name, inputs, required fields. we also recommend post-parse validation and a small fallback handler to map close variants like userEmail -> user_email.
[03:38] Liam: are these mapping heuristics part of the SDK?
[03:41] Derek: yes, the SDK includes a thin adapter and a checksum-based schema validator, but it's opt-in. we can send you sample code in python and ts.
[03:50] Maya: the malformed JSON caused a retry storm in prod the other day. we had our orchestrator requeue on parse error and that multiplied load.
[04:02] Samira: that's an important operational note — add idempotency keys and short-circuit on known schema errors to avoid retries. also set a backoff.
[04:15] Priya: question on graceful degradation: if the function call fails, can we fall back to a canned response or lower-fidelity model?
[04:23] Derek: yes you can define fallback policy: e.g., if the mid-tier quantized fails or latency > 1s, route to base-tier hosted or a cached answer. Redwood's routing policy can do that.
[04:36] Maya: what's the cost delta when we route to base-tier hosted? ballpark.
[04:41] Samira: roughly 2-3x per token. we'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[04:48] Speaker 1: ok noted.
[04:53] Derek: another cause of p99 is our function-calling overhead when large tool outputs are embedded in the response; serializing big JSONs increases token count and compute time. consider streaming partial tool outputs where possible.
[05:11] Liam: about the KV cache — is there a way to pin certain user sessions to keep cache hot?
[05:18] Derek: yes session affinity plus prefix pinning helps. we can set a session key to prefer a warm cache, but that reduces global packing efficiency.
[05:29] Maya: can you remind us of the recommended TTL vs expected prompt length? we have multi-turns around 120 tokens average.
[05:35] Derek: for ~120 tokens, a TTL of 60s was working in our tests, but if you have quick back-and-forth shorter TTL or sticky sessions. we'll recommend TTLs in the doc.
[05:46] Samira: let's go through the specific run numbers you sent.
[06:00] Maya: right — run A was with batch window 15ms, run B 40ms, run C 40ms + sticky sessions. run A p95 620ms p99 1.4s. run B p95 540ms p99 1.2s. run C p95 510ms p99 720ms.
[06:25] Derek: run C shows the sticky sessions drastically reduce p99 because of cache locality. cost goes up slightly due to less packing.
[06:33] Priya: so run C looks best for our UX. what's the cost estimate?
[06:38] Samira: i estimated about 12% higher per-token cost, i'll publish the spreadsheet.
[06:45] Speaker 4: side note on function-calling — we noticed sometimes the model invents new function names instead of calling the registered one.
[06:54] Derek: that's model hallucination for tool names; best mitigation is to provide clear system prompts and limit function list to the minimum. also prefer structured function definitions with types.
[07:07] Maya: about the malformed outputs — can the SDK auto-normalize key names?
[07:11] Derek: we have a small normalization layer that maps synonyms, but it can't cover everything. better is strict schema validation and quick fallback.
[07:21] Liam: security question — KMS integration for private deployments: do you support customer-managed keys in the private control plane?
[07:30] Samira: yes for private we support KMS/HSM, for Dedicated we can do customer-managed KMS integration; we'll confirm exact vendors supported in the security doc.
[07:43] Maya: we also need SOC2 + ISO documentation and network diagrams for our compliance team.
[07:50] Samira: noted — i'll send the security pack.
[07:56] Priya: quick perf question: can we do a canary routing so 10% of traffic hits the new config?
[08:02] Derek: yes, Redwood Console supports percent-based rollouts and can automatically fallback if latency deviates. we can show the console in next demo.
[08:12] Maya: one more operational — during retry storms, our orchestrator retried on 5xx from Redwood which caused loops. is there a recommended error code to short-circuit?
[08:24] Derek: we recommend returning 422 for parse/schema errors to avoid retry logic, and 503 for transient infra errors. also include a Retry-After header in 503s.
[08:36] Speaker 1: that's helpful.
[08:40] Samira: i'll summarize next steps: we'll send tuned configs, sample SDK adapter, and perf spreadsheet. greenline runs staging load tests. security team sync for KMS and compliance.
[08:53] Maya: sounds good. any blockers on sending the code samples?
[08:57] Derek: none, i'll attach python + ts snippets and a small dockerized check tool.
[09:05] Priya: can we also get a small example of graceful degrade flow with canned answers?
[09:11] Samira: yes, derek will include a sample fallback handler.
[09:16] Liam: timeline-wise we'll aim to run the load tests this week and update by monday.
[09:21] Samira: perfect. last question — are we comfortable with the decision to stick with quantized mid-tier vs switching to full baseline?
[09:29] Maya: based on run C i'd say keep mid-tier with sticky sessions for now.
[09:35] Samira: ok we'll proceed. thanks all, i'll follow up with the artifacts.
[09:40] (crosstalk, meeting ends)

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-attributions and auto-caption errors ("kv cash", "userEmail" variations). Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/perf-spreadsheet (perf spreadsheet), https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (security docs), ticket #1234 (function contract).

End of transcript.
